title: Surface Areas & Volumes
description: Class 9 IMO — Surface Areas & Volumes: cuboid and cube, cylinder, cone, sphere and hemisphere — their curved/total surface areas and volumes, plus simple combinations of solids.

topics.title: Cuboid and Cube
topics.concept:
What are 3D Solids?

Three-dimensional (3D) solids have length, breadth (width), and height. They occupy space.

Definitions:

  • Surface Area: The total area of all faces of a 3D solid (square units)
  • Lateral Surface Area (LSA): Area of only the side faces (excluding top and bottom)
  • Total Surface Area (TSA): Area of all faces including top and bottom
  • Volume: The amount of space inside a 3D solid (cubic units)

Cube (all sides equal = a):

MeasurementFormula
Total Surface Area (TSA)\(6a^2\)
Volume\(a^3\)

Cuboid (length = l, breadth = b, height = h):

MeasurementFormula
Total Surface Area (TSA)\(2(lb + bh + hl)\)
Volume\(l \times b \times h\)
recap: Cuboid: TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl), V = lbh.

quiz.q: The lateral surface area of a cube is 256 m². The volume of the cube is:
quiz.explanation: LSA of cube = 4a² = 256. Therefore, a² = 64 → a = 8 m. Volume = a³ = 8³ = 512 m³.

quiz.q: The radius of a spherical balloon increases from 7 cm to 14 cm as air is being pumped into it. Find the ratio of surface areas of the balloon in the two cases.
quiz.explanation: Initial radius r₁ = 7 cm. Final radius r₂ = 14 cm. Surface area = 4πr². Ratio = 4πr₁² / 4πr₂² = (r₁/r₂)² = (7/14)² = (1/2)² = 1:4.

topics.title: Cylinder and Cone
topics.concept:
What are Cylinder and Cone?

  • Cylinder: A 3D solid with two parallel circular bases connected by a curved surface
  • Cone: A 3D solid with a circular base and a curved surface tapering to a point (vertex)

Right Circular Cylinder (radius = r, height = h):

MeasurementFormula
Total Surface Area (TSA)\(2\pi r(r + h)\)
Volume\(\pi r^2 h\)

Right Circular Cone (radius = r, height = h, slant height = l):

MeasurementFormula
Curved Surface Area (CSA)\(\pi r l\)
Total Surface Area (TSA)\(\pi r(r + l)\)
Volume\(\frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h\)

Important Notes:

  • π ≈ 3.14 or 22/7
  • CSA is also called lateral surface area
  • For cone, l (slant height) is NOT the same as h (vertical height)
recap: Cone: l = √(r² + h²), CSA = πrl, V = ⅓πr²h.

quiz.q: The curved surface area of a right circular cone of height 15 cm and base diameter 16 cm is:
quiz.explanation: Diameter = 16 → r = 8 cm. Height h = 15 cm. Slant height l = √(8² + 15²) = √(64 + 225) = √289 = 17 cm. CSA = πrl = π(8)(17) = 136π cm².

topics.title: Sphere and Hemisphere
topics.concept:
A sphere of radius r has surface area 4πr² and volume (4/3)πr². A hemisphere has curved surface area 2πr², total surface area 3πr² (curved plus the flat circle), and volume (2/3)πr².

Combined solids (a cone on a hemisphere, a capsule, etc.) are handled by adding the relevant surface areas or volumes.

examples.problem: Surface area of a sphere of radius 7 (π = 22/7)?

examples.solution: Curved 2πr² plus the flat circular face πr² gives 3πr².

quiz.q: A 20 m deep well with diameter 7 m is dug and the earth from digging is evenly spread out to form a platform 22 m by 14 m. Find the height of the platform.
quiz.explanation: Volume of earth dug out = Volume of cylindrical well = πr²h = (22/7) × (3.5)² × 20 = (22/7) × 12.25 × 20 = 770 m³. Volume of platform = l × b × h = 22 × 14 × h = 308h. 308h = 770 → h = 770 / 308 = 2.5 m.

quiz.q: Find the length of canvas 2 m in width required to make a conical tent 12 m in diameter and 63 m in slant height.
quiz.explanation: Diameter = 12 m, so r = 6 m. l = 63 m. CSA = πrl = (22/7) × 6 × 63 = 22 × 6 × 9 = 1188 m². Length × Width = Area. Length × 2 = 1188 → Length = 594 m.

questions.q: A heap of wheat is in the form of a cone of diameter 10.5 m and height 3 m. Find the area of the canvas required to just cover the heap. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Radius r = 10.5/2 = 5.25 m and height h = 3 m. Slant height l = √(r² + h²) = √(27.5625 + 9) = √36.5625 ≈ 6.05 m. Canvas needed = curved surface area = πrl = (22/7) × 5.25 × 6.05 ≈ 99.83 m².

questions.q: If the length of the diagonal of a cube is 8√3 cm, then its surface area is:
questions.explanation: Diagonal of a cube = a√3. So, a√3 = 8√3 → a = 8 cm. TSA = 6a² = 6 × 8² = 6 × 64 = 384 cm².

questions.q: If a right circular cone has radius 5 cm and slant height 13 cm, what is its volume?
questions.explanation: Radius r = 5, slant height l = 13. Height h = √(l² - r²) = √(169 - 25) = √144 = 12 cm. Volume = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π(25)(12) = 100π cm³.

questions.q: Three metal cubes of edges 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm are melted and cast into a single cube. The edge of the new cube is:
questions.explanation: Volume of new cube = 3³ + 4³ + 5³ = 27 + 64 + 125 = 216 cm³. Since V = a³, a = ∛216 = 6 cm.

questions.q: A capsule is in the shape of a cylinder with two hemispheres stuck to each of its ends. The length of the entire capsule is 14 mm and the diameter of the capsule is 5 mm. Find its surface area.
questions.explanation: Radius r = 2.5 mm. Length of cylindrical part = Total length - 2(radius) = 14 - 2(2.5) = 14 - 5 = 9 mm. Total Surface Area = CSA of cylinder + 2 × CSA of hemisphere = 2πrh + 2(2πr²) = 2πr(h + 2r) = 2 × (22/7) × 2.5 × (9 + 5) = 2 × (22/7) × 2.5 × 14 = 220 mm².

questions.q: If a right circular cylinder and a right circular cone have the same radius and same volume, then the ratio of the height of the cylinder to the height of the cone is:
questions.explanation: V_cylinder = πr²h₁. V_cone = (1/3)πr²h₂. Since they are equal: πr²h₁ = (1/3)πr²h₂ → h₁ = (1/3)h₂ → h₁/h₂ = 1/3. Ratio is 1:3.

questions.q: The cost of painting the total outside surface of a closed cylindrical oil tank at ₹60 per sq. m is ₹237.60. The height of the tank is 6 times the radius of the base of the tank. Find its volume.
questions.explanation: Total surface area = cost ÷ rate = 237.60 ÷ 60 = 3.96 m². With h = 6r, TSA = 2πr(r + h) = 2πr(7r) = 14πr² = 44r², so 44r² = 3.96, r² = 0.09 and r = 0.3 m (h = 1.8 m). Volume = πr²h = (22/7) × 0.09 × 1.8 ≈ 0.509 m³.

questions.q: If a sphere and a cube have the same surface area, then the ratio of the volume of the sphere to the volume of the cube is:
questions.explanation: Surface areas equal: 4πr² = 6a² → a² = (4π/6)r² = (2π/3)r² → a = r√(2π/3). Ratio of volumes = (4/3)πr³ / a³ = (4/3)πr³ / (r³(2π/3)√(2π/3)) = (4/3)π / ((2π/3)√(2π/3)) = 2 / √(2π/3) = √6 / √π = √6 : √π.

questions.q: Two cubes each of volume 64 cm³ are joined end to end. The surface area of the resulting cuboid is:
questions.explanation: Volume of one cube = 64 cm³ → side a = 4 cm. When joined, length of cuboid l = 4+4 = 8 cm, breadth b = 4 cm, height h = 4 cm. TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl) = 2(32 + 16 + 32) = 2(80) = 160 cm².

questions.q: A hemispherical bowl is made of steel, 0.25 cm thick. The inner radius of the bowl is 5 cm. The outer curved surface area of the bowl is:
questions.explanation: Inner radius r = 5 cm, thickness = 0.25 cm. Outer radius R = 5 + 0.25 = 5.25 cm. Outer CSA = 2πR² = 2 × (22/7) × 5.25 × 5.25 = 2 × 22 × 0.75 × 5.25 = 173.25 cm².
